rules.title: name!(...) callee must be a #[fn_macro] or #[token_macro] fn
rules.statement: A `name!(...)` invocation resolves `name` against the function overload set; the callee selected must be a fn annotated `#[fn_macro]` or `#[token_macro]`. If `name` is unknown, or no overload bears such an annotation, the call is rejected. Only macro-annotated fns are callable via `name!(...)` syntax.
rules.uncertainty: Resolution is restricted to non-generic funcs_ (generic fn_macro out of scope for this slice).

rules.title: Accepted fn-macro/token-macro signatures
rules.statement: A `#[fn_macro]` callee must have exactly one parameter and signature `(ExprBlob) -> ExprBlob` (single-arg form) or `(Vec<ExprBlob>) -> ExprBlob` (N-arg packed form). A `#[token_macro]` callee must have signature `(str) -> ExprBlob`. Any other signature is rejected.

rules.title: Single-arg fn-macro takes exactly one argument
rules.statement: For a callee with signature `(ExprBlob) -> ExprBlob`, the `name!(...)` invocation must supply exactly one argument; supplying any other count is an error.

rules.title: name!(...) arguments parse as a comma-separated expression list
rules.statement: The raw text between the parentheses of `name!(...)` is parsed as a comma-separated list of expressions (each becoming one macro ARG). If it does not parse as such, the invocation is rejected.

rules.title: Each fn-macro argument is passed as its serialized AST subtree (ExprBlob)
rules.statement: Each argument expression of `name!(...)` is passed to the callee unevaluated as an `ExprBlob` referencing the serialized AST subtree of that argument; the callee receives the syntax tree, not a runtime value. For the Vec form, all argument ExprBlobs are packed into a `Vec<ExprBlob>` in source order.

rules.title: token-macro receives unparsed raw text as str
rules.statement: For a `#[token_macro]` callee, the raw bytes between the delimiters of `name!(...)` are forwarded verbatim as a single `str` argument, bypassing expression-list parsing and per-argument AST serialization.

rules.title: fn-macro call expands to the ExprBlob it returns
rules.statement: A `name!(...)` expression has the callee's return type `ExprBlob`; at expansion the AST produced by the macro (the returned ExprBlob) is spliced in place of the call site before final sema.

rules.title: cfg!(...) is a compile-time built-in predicate
rules.statement: The built-in macro `cfg!(...)` is evaluated at compile (sema) time to a bool literal, before user fn-macro resolution. It accepts built-in target keys, the boolean combinators `all`/`any`/`not`, and user feature flags supplied via `--cfg`.

rules.title: Format-family macros validate a literal format string at compile time
rules.statement: For the format family (`format`, `print`, `println`, `eprint`, `eprintln`, `panic`, `format_args_str`) and the write family (`write`, `writeln`), when the format-string argument is a string literal it is parsed and validated at sema time (brace balance, placeholder structure). A non-literal format-string argument skips the check (mirroring Rust `format_args!`). The format string is arg[0] for the format family and arg[1] for the write family.

rules.title: Format placeholder count must match the argument count
rules.statement: When no explicit `{N}` index appears, the number of value placeholders in the format string must equal the number of value arguments provided (args after the format string, and after the sink for write/writeln). When explicit indices are used, the number of value arguments must be at least max(explicit-index)+1. Otherwise the macro is rejected.

rules.title: Each format placeholder dispatches to its format-trait method
rules.statement: Each format placeholder lowers to a call dispatching to the format trait selected by the placeholder's trait kind (e.g. `{}` -> Display, `{:?}` -> Debug, plus hex/oct/bin/exp variants), invoked on the argument value with a `&mut Formatter`. Per-placeholder format spec fields (fill, alignment, sign, alternate, zero-pad, width, precision) are applied to the Formatter before each dispatch and reset between placeholders.

rules.title: Format-family expansion builds a String/Formatter block
rules.statement: format!/format_args_str! expand to a block yielding a `String` built via a `Formatter` over a `__buf`. The print family (`println`/`print`/`eprintln`/`eprint`) appends a drain of the buffer to stdout/stderr; `panic!` drains to a panic. write!/writeln! build a `Formatter` directly over the sink (via `(sink).as_formatter()`), stream placeholders into it, and yield `Result<(),Error>` (always Ok — per-placeholder errors are discarded); writeln! additionally writes a trailing newline.

rules.title: Format/write macros require a format-string argument
rules.statement: A format-family or write-family invocation must supply at least the format-string argument; an empty argument list is an error.
